about: Questions a person would actually ask of a repository, with the right answer named
in advance by opening the source -- never by running graph-paat and accepting what it
said. Ten per corpus. `why` records how the answer was decided, so a disputed question
can be re-argued from the same evidence rather than from memory.
An answer is written as `path/to/file.ext:Label`, matching a node in the built graph.
More than one answer is listed only where two symbols are genuinely equally correct --
a library that ships two major versions side by side, for instance -- and the reason
is written into `why`. Every extra answer makes the question easier, so they are rare.
Scored by tests/question_runner.py: is the named answer the FIRST result, and is it in
the top three. Run `python -m tests.question_runner` to see every miss.

lua-telescope.q: how do I build a source that runs a program a single time and reuses its output
lua-telescope.why: finders.lua:L189-215 splits the command list and hands fn_command to async_oneshot_finder, whose job_started guard (async_oneshot_finder.lua:L35-56) spawns only once

lua-telescope.q: how are the columns in each result row assigned their widths
lua-telescope.why: entry_display.lua:L66-95 builds one generator per configured item, resolving v.width through resolve.resolve_width and padding with strings.align_str

lua-telescope.q: what keeps the running count above the prompt from redrawing on every incoming match
lua-telescope.why: pickers.lua:L580 wraps get_status_updater in debounce.throttle_leading(status_updater, 50); debounce.lua:L19-33 fires on the leading edge then drops calls for 50ms

php-slim.q: how does a browser form pretend to be a delete or a put
php-slim.why: Middleware/MethodOverrideMiddleware.php:L26 reads the X-Http-Method-Override header, and L30-L35 falls back to a _METHOD field inside a POST body; nothing else in the tree rewrites the request method.

php-slim.q: how does the framework tell the client how many bytes the body is
php-slim.why: Middleware/ContentLengthMiddleware.php:L26-L29 takes getBody()->getSize() and sets the Content-Length header when the response does not already carry one.

php-slim.q: what captures text echoed by a handler before it reaches the page
php-slim.why: Middleware/OutputBufferingMiddleware.php:L55-L57 wraps the inner handler in ob_start/ob_get_clean, and L63-L70 appends or prepends the captured string to the response body.

php-slim.q: where does incoming json become a php array
php-slim.why: Middleware/BodyParsingMiddleware.php:L99-L108 registers the application/json parser built on json_decode($input, true), and L55 process() attaches the result as the parsed body.

php-slim.q: how do I make a link that already includes the application base path
php-slim.why: Routing/RouteParser.php:L104-L113 is the only builder that prefixes routeCollector->getBasePath(); relativeUrlFor (L40) omits it and fullUrlFor (L119) adds scheme and authority on top of urlFor.

php-slim.q: how does it work out from the request whether an error should come back as html or plain text
php-slim.why: Handlers/ErrorHandler.php:L172-L191 intersects the Accept header with the registered renderer keys and breaks the tie away from text/plain; determineRenderer (L216) only maps the already-chosen type to a renderer.

php-slim.q: why does a 204 send nothing at all to the client
php-slim.why: ResponseEmitter.php:L124-L128 returns true for status 204, 205 and 304, and emit() at L50-L52 skips emitBody entirely when it does.

php-slim.q: how can path placeholders arrive as individual positional parameters
php-slim.why: Handlers/Strategies/RequestResponseArgs.php:L29 spreads array_values($routeArguments) positionally; the sibling RequestResponseNamedArgs.php:L28 spreads the associative array as named arguments instead, so 'positional' picks exactly one.

php-slim.q: how does a nested group get the outer prefix glued onto its pattern
php-slim.why: Routing/RouteCollectorProxy.php:L177 does $pattern = $this->groupPattern . $pattern before delegating; RouteCollector::group (L230) creates the group object but never concatenates the prefix.

php-slim.q: which exception carries the list of methods allowed for a path
php-slim.why: Exception/HttpMethodNotAllowedException.php:L20 holds $allowedMethods with the getter at L38 and code 405 at L25; Middleware/RoutingMiddleware.php:L79-L81 fills it from the routing results.

ruby-rack.q: how does it work out which client address to trust when proxies sit in front
ruby-rack.why: rack/request.rb:L508 walks REMOTE_ADDR backwards returning the first untrusted address, then falls back to the forwarded-for chain at L515; the ip at L67 is a one-line delegate to this one

ruby-rack.q: how does the app shrink what it sends back so less travels over the wire
ruby-rack.why: rack/deflater.rb:L28 class, doc at L12 'content encoding of http responses, usually for purposes of compression'; L57 call picks the encoding and wraps the body in GzipStream

ruby-rack.q: what tries a list of apps in order until one of them actually answers
ruby-rack.why: rack/cascade.rb:L11 class, doc at L6 'tries a request on several apps, and returns the first response that is not 404 or 405'; L32 call loops over @apps

ruby-rack.q: what stops two threads from running through the application at the same moment
ruby-rack.why: rack/lock.rb:L8 class, doc at L6 'locks every request inside a mutex'; L13 call takes @mutex.lock and releases it via a BodyProxy

ruby-rack.q: how can a plain html form pretend to be a delete or a put
ruby-rack.why: rack/method_override.rb:L8 class; the _method form field at L15 and the X-HTTP-Method-Override header at L16 are read by method_override at L41 and rewritten into REQUEST_METHOD at L34

ruby-rack.q: how does it guess what kind of content a served file holds from its name ending
ruby-rack.why: rack/mime.rb:L18 fetches the '.ext' key out of MIME_TYPES with a fallback; rack/files.rb:L223 has a same-named helper but it just delegates here

ruby-rack.q: how do i get at the cookies a browser sent along with a request
ruby-rack.why: rack/request.rb:L378 caches a parsed hash under RACK_REQUEST_COOKIE_HASH and refills it from Utils.parse_cookies_header when the raw string changes; the request side is what the question asks for, not the utils helper

ruby-rack.q: how does it find the boundary marker inside a multipart content type header
ruby-rack.why: rack/multipart/parser.rb:L122 matches MULTIPART against the content type and returns capture 2, raising BoundaryTooLongError when a second boundary parameter follows

ruby-rack.q: how do i mount several different apps under different url prefixes
ruby-rack.why: rack/urlmap.rb:L20 class, doc at L8 'takes a hash mapping urls or paths to apps, and dispatches accordingly'; remap at L25 sorts longest location first

ruby-rack.q: how does it check whether the cached copy a browser already holds is still fresh
ruby-rack.why: rack/conditional_get.rb:L52 checks if-none-match first then if-modified-since; call at L34 turns a true result into a 304 with an emptied body

rust-ripgrep.q: how does it decide that a file is not text and stop reading it
rust-ripgrep.why: searcher/src/searcher/mod.rs:L55 — the type whose none/quit/convert constructors (L62, L81, L98) pick the strategy for spotting non-text data and ending the search as if at EOF

rust-ripgrep.q: how does it decide whether to load an entire file into memory at once instead of reading it in pieces
rust-ripgrep.why: searcher/src/searcher/mmap.rs:L13 — doc at L5 says it 'Controls the strategy used for determining when to use memory maps'; auto() at L48, never() at L54

rust-ripgrep.q: what does a caller implement to receive every hit as the search produces it
rust-ripgrep.why: searcher/src/sink.rs:L102 — the trait callers implement; its matched method at L124 is documented as 'called whenever a match is found'

rust-ripgrep.q: how does searching work when a match is allowed to span several lines
rust-ripgrep.why: searcher/src/searcher/glue.rs:L142 — the third search strategy alongside ReadByLine (L11) and SliceByLine (L97); its new() at L149 asserts searcher.multi_line_with_matcher

rust-ripgrep.q: how do I get one machine readable record per match instead of the usual output
rust-ripgrep.why: printer/src/json.rs:L487 - the JSON Lines printer; its doc block at L470-L484 shows the one-object-per-match records it emits, sibling of Standard (standard.rs:L480) and Summary (summary.rs:L349)

rust-ripgrep.q: how are directories crawled using more than one thread at a time
rust-ripgrep.why: ignore/src/walk.rs:L1411 — the type returned by WalkBuilder::build_parallel (L701); its visit() at L1452 spawns the worker threads

rust-ripgrep.q: where does it look up the user's global list of files to skip
rust-ripgrep.why: ignore/src/gitignore.rs:L583 — doc at L580 'Return the file path of the current environment's global gitignore file'; it reads GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, then $HOME/.gitconfig, then XDG, then system config

rust-ripgrep.q: what decides whether a path passes the include and exclude patterns typed on the command line
rust-ripgrep.why: ignore/src/overrides.rs:L47 — doc at L45 'Manages a set of overrides provided explicitly by the end user'; its matched() at L96 answers for one path

rust-ripgrep.q: how does it go faster by pulling a plain string out of the pattern first
rust-ripgrep.why: regex/src/literal.rs:L40 — doc at L19-L23 describes searching for the literal, finding the bounds of the line it occurs in, then running the original regex on only that line

rust-ripgrep.q: how is the text of a match rewritten before it gets printed
rust-ripgrep.why: printer/src/util.rs:L14 — doc at L13 'A type for handling replacements while amortizing allocation'; replace_all() at L51 does the substitution the printers then emit

swift-alamofire.q: which type watches for the device switching between wifi and cellular
swift-alamofire.why: Features/NetworkReachabilityManager.swift:L41 class decl; doc L30-31 says it listens for reachability changes for both cellular and WiFi interfaces, and L61-66 defines ConnectionType .ethernetOrWiFi / .cellular. Only type in the corpus that reports link type.

swift-alamofire.q: what holds a failed call until the internet comes back
swift-alamofire.why: Features/OfflineRetrier.swift:L29-31 doc: uses NWPathMonitor to detect when connectivity is restored to retry failed requests; L50-58 pendingCompletions plus a timeoutWorkItem hold the retry decision open.

swift-alamofire.q: what refreshes an expired token and queues other calls while it happens
swift-alamofire.why: Features/AuthenticationInterceptor.swift:L158-160 doc: manages the queuing and threading complexity of authenticating requests and Credential refresh; L216-219 adaptOperations / requestsToRetry are the queues.

swift-alamofire.q: how do I keep a value safe when two threads write to it at once
swift-alamofire.why: Core/Protected.swift:L83-84 doc 'A thread-safe wrapper around a value'; L101 read and L110 write both go through lock.around. UnfairLock (L55) is the lock itself, not the wrapper a caller uses.

swift-alamofire.q: how are the underlying system jobs matched back to the objects that started them
swift-alamofire.why: Core/RequestTaskMap.swift:L27-28 doc: maintains a two way, one to one map of URLSessionTasks to Requests; L31-33 holds both directions plus per-task event flags.

swift-alamofire.q: how does it wait longer and longer between attempts after something fails
swift-alamofire.why: Features/RetryPolicy.swift:L27-29 doc says exponential backoff; L33 defaultExponentialBackoffBase = 2 and L36 defaultExponentialBackoffScale = 0.5 are the growth knobs.

swift-alamofire.q: how do I pin a certificate so the app trusts only my own server
swift-alamofire.why: Features/ServerTrustEvaluation.swift:L229 class decl; doc L224-227 describes certificate pinning against bundled certificates. PublicKeysTrustEvaluator (L320) pins keys, not certificates, so the certificate wording picks one.

swift-alamofire.q: are header names compared without regard to capitalization
swift-alamofire.why: Core/HTTPHeaders.swift:L27-28 doc 'order-preserving and case-insensitive representation of HTTP headers'; L92 sort uses lowercased() and L110 value(for:) looks up via the case-insensitive index(of:).

swift-alamofire.q: how do I attach a file and some form fields to one upload
swift-alamofire.why: Features/MultipartFormData.swift:L45 class decl; L148 append(_ data:withName:) and L172 append(_ fileURL:withName:) are the caller-facing builders. MultipartUpload (Features/MultipartUpload.swift:L28) is marked 'Internal type' and only wraps this one.

swift-alamofire.q: how do I stream a response as it arrives instead of waiting for the whole body
swift-alamofire.why: Core/DataStreamRequest.swift:L26-27 doc: Request subclass which streams HTTP response Data through a Handler closure; L34 Stream and L48 Event carry each chunk.
